$description: Design tokens, in the W3C Design Tokens Format Module shape (v2025.10). THE authority for every design value in the product. packages/tokens/generated/tokens.css is DERIVED from this file and is never hand-edited (law 27). Three layers, and the middle one is the point: primitives are raw values, semantics name a ROLE, and components reference semantics. A screen that reaches past the semantic layer to a primitive has hardcoded a decision the design system is supposed to own.

color.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. Raw values with no opinion about use. Never referenced by a component or a screen -- only by the semantic layer below.

space.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. A 4px scale, so spacing is chosen from a set rather than invented per screen.

font.$description: PRIMITIVE layer. A system stack: no web font on the critical path, because the performance budget is 180KB of critical-path JS and a font is the easiest way to spend a chunk of it for nothing.

sans.$value: ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

semantic.$description: SEMANTIC layer. Names a ROLE, not a value. This is the layer components and screens are allowed to use, and the reason a theme change is a token change rather than a sweep through every screen.

danger.$description: For a state that has gone wrong. NOT for a destructive action button, which needs its own role when one exists.

warning.$description: For a state the user must reconcile -- a version conflict, a stale projection. Distinct from danger: nothing is broken, but something needs a decision.

focus.$description: The focus ring is a token, so it cannot be styled away per screen. Keyboard operability is a property of the system, not a per-component courtesy.
